requirements.requirement: Keep things tidy: separate places for different items
requirements.evidence: Seven separate compartments plus one open bin across the 3 bases. The open faces have end caps and the joints are bolted (capOpenFaces, lockJoints). check_build found no rule issues and the meshClash check reads clear.
The catalogue has no sewing props (no thread, scissors or pins). Stand-ins are placed instead: a marker, pen, paint brush, tape measure and tweezers.

finish.summary: I built a small three-cell sewing organiser for a tabletop. It has three full-depth bins and a small corner bin, so different supplies each have their own space. The open faces have end caps and the joints are bolted. check_build found no rule issues and no parts colliding (meshClash: clear). It's 17 printed parts, about 1786 g of filament and about 40 hours of printing. The catalogue has no sewing props, so I used stand-ins to show how it's used: a marker and a pen stand in the 3-compartment bin, a paint brush in the 2-compartment bin, a tape measure in the open bin and tweezers in the small corner bin. The tape measure and tweezers ended up standing on end because they didn't fit lying down.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
